tasks.title: Adopt bootstrap release records in native change roles
tasks.goal: Reuse the already retained change identities and evidence when M-02 change documents become available.
steps: After the root-bound M-02 prerequisites, inspect their actual immutable ID grammar and document-role registration. Adopt each bootstrap record as the release-impact non-normative evidence role of the same change; do not mint replacement IDs or create a second change directory family.

Reconcile PROP-058 only where necessary to describe that evidence role and exclusion from normative intent/work subject hashing. Preserve release-impact file bytes and immutable IDs during adoption; make any separately justified format evolution an explicit registered transition.

Bind paths using the configured spec root and accepted M-02 ownership rules. Register the role in the existing parser/manifest path, with only the required module exports; do not introduce runtime done/owner/current fields or a competing plan.

Add regression fixtures proving that adding or updating release-impact evidence does not change intent/work identities or create a self-closing normative dependency. Verify all retained capture, contribution and capability references still resolve.
positive_cases: A bootstrap record is discoverable through the native change role without identity or byte changes.
Changing evidence after an accepted contribution leaves its intent/work subject unchanged.
negative_cases: A release-impact record declared normative, moved to a new synthetic identity or included in its own closure subject is refused.
An escaping role path or an unknown evidence epoch cannot be silently accepted.
checks: TO CREATE/USE AFTER BASE.2: python -B -m unittest discover -s tools/preview-transition/tests -p test_*.py
TO CREATE/USE AFTER BASE.2: python -B tools/preview-transition/check.py --transition docs/releases/developer-preview-1-to-2/transition.json --mode bindings --stage roles --format json
acceptance: All retained bootstrap IDs and bytes survive adoption with exact before/after witnesses.
Native change analysis and permanent accounting tools read the same records; no second ledger acquires authority.
tasks.safe_stop: Stop once native role adoption and identity preservation pass; migration/facade binding belongs to BIND.2.
tasks.commit_subject: feat(change): adopt preview impacts as change evidence
notes: NEXT-A26 is the temporary design unit supplied by the root packet. Read its accepted permanent replacement after promotion. PROP-068 is PROPOSED until BASE.2 creates it; BASE.1 reads the temporary capture rule and must not claim a missing permanent file exists. Create permanent law before production code or tests cite its anchors.

Only listed outer write roots may change. Proposed paths are not claims of existing files. Narrow configured spec-root change records and documentation paths to the actual accepted binding before dispatch; refine the packet if a necessary path is outside that perimeter.

Permanent release records use immutable change IDs, capability/topic IDs and exact captures, never NEXT task IDs as product identity. The temporary task-to-change bridge is execution evidence and is removed at campaign retirement.

TO CREATE checks name future obligations and must not be reported as existing or passing. BASE.2 defines and tests their exact command grammar; later packets use that accepted grammar. A missing validator, zero selected tests or unavailable platform is an unmet check.

Keep NEXT-EXECUTION-AUTHORITY blocked during planning. These tasks do not authorize public publication, host installation, version bumps, prototype graduation, new IDE clients or an autonomous scheduler.

Verification follows the current multi-user-planning economy: run required affected checks against exact inputs; mutation testing is optional only for a concrete suspicious signal and a bounded cheaper proof, never a ritual for every contribution.

tasks.title: Connect format migrations and capability surfaces to release impacts
tasks.goal: Link existing domain-owned change machinery to the permanent release record without duplicating journals or protocols.
steps: After the accepted M-13-C and M-16-C foundations named by the DAG, resolve each relevant format-break record, migration operation descriptor and capability coverage row by its actual permanent identity and exact schema/source capture.

Extend accounting references and checker consistency rules to those existing records. Migration plans, apply journals and capability schemas remain owned by their existing domains; the release record stores links and conclusions rather than copying their event stream or inventing an alternative migration operation.

Distinguish automatic authored conversion, manual authored changes, rebuild/re-fetch of derived data, explicit no action and unsupported transitions. A migration recipe is automatic only when its implemented command and preconditions are backed by exact evidence.

Check that machine readers can join the same canonical change/capture/capability records and report stale or missing links. Record additions as well as changed and removed surfaces, including semantics that have no format break note.
positive_cases: A format break, its real migration descriptor and affected capability join to one release impact.
A new capability with no format break still creates an explicit documentation obligation.
negative_cases: A copied prose recipe cannot masquerade as an implemented automatic converter.
A dangling or stale migration descriptor, missing new capability or second wire journal blocks binding.
Schema-only exposure is not counted as operational coverage.
checks: TO CREATE/USE AFTER BASE.2: python -B -m unittest discover -s tools/preview-transition/tests -p test_*.py

acceptance: All applicable migration and capability links resolve to their domain-owned permanent records and exact supported behavior.
Release accounting is mechanically readable without a new IDE client, universal operation protocol or duplicated runtime journal.
tasks.safe_stop: Stop after reference consistency and classifications are evidenced; complete guidance awaits the final candidate.
